instruction: For a museum catalogue audit, use the public taxonomic catalogue covering all living reptiles, as available on 9 September 2026. Consider currently accepted species whose exact genus is Chelodina and whose original description year is before 1900. Find the type account that says a former British Museum catalogue number is identified in the museum accession books as a species outside Chelodina. Resolve that referred name to its currently accepted species. For that species' exact current genus, list every currently accepted species originally described before 1900. Report each accepted binomial, original description year, and the catalogue identifier of its own holotype; exclude type specimens attributed only to synonyms or subspecies. Sort by accepted binomial. A complete accepted-species checklist can establish the initial genus-and-year pool. Inspect those type accounts for the accession-book referral, then use the referred accepted record to determine the later genus filter. Use exact genus membership because a broad name search can include longer genus names.
output_format: Return only a pipe-separated table with header accepted_species|description_year|holotype_catalogue. Use one row per accepted species, a four-digit year, and the institution prefix plus catalogue number for the holotype.
